cards.v: We love him, because he first loved us.
cards.a: Write down three signs that you have seen God's love for you today, and read them to the Lord before you sleep.

cards.v: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
cards.a: Before bed, ask yourself: What filled my heart today? Hand it over to the Lord.

cards.v: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
cards.a: Turn off your phone for ten minutes and speak only to the Lord, asking for no particular result.

cards.v: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
cards.a: When someone tests your patience, pause for three seconds before you respond and say in your heart: Lord, not me, but You.

cards.v: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
cards.a: In one small matter, let the other person choose first: what to eat, where to go, how to plan it.

cards.v: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
cards.a: Write one fear you have about relationships to the Lord, then say: I give it to You.

cards.v: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
cards.a: Admit one mistake today. Simply say, "I'm sorry, that was my fault," with no excuses.

cards.t: Love the Lord with All Your Heart
cards.v: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
cards.a: Spend ten minutes alone with God today before you answer any messages.

cards.v: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
cards.a: Send a specific word of encouragement to a friend: "I really admire you for..."

cards.v: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath,
cards.a: When you feel angry, step away first and cool down. If you feel unsafe, reach out right away to someone you trust. Do not face it alone.

cards.v: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
cards.a: Choose one area to do better in today (speech, conduct, or purity) and tell your companion.

cards.t: How Can a Young Person Stay Pure?
cards.v: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
cards.a: Write down your boundaries and say them aloud to a companion, and agree to check in with each other every week.

cards.t: Set Nothing Wicked Before Your Eyes
cards.v: I will set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of faithless men. They will not cling to me.
cards.a: Delete or hide one account, group, or app that makes you weak.

cards.v: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
cards.a: If you stumble, don't hide. Confess to God, then tell one trusted companion, and begin again from today.

cards.v: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
cards.a: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and focus on bearing it toward one person today.

cards.v: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
cards.a: The next time you feel like arguing, slow down for three seconds, then speak in a gentle tone.

cards.v: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
cards.a: Find a spiritual companion. Share one struggle with each other and pray for one another.

cards.v: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
cards.a: Tell two mature people about one relationship decision and listen to their advice.

cards.v: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
cards.a: Ask someone you trust: What do you see in me that I should pay attention to?

cards.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
cards.a: Write down one old wound and say to the Lord: I choose to forgive. (Forgiving does not mean trusting again right away.)

cards.v: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
cards.a: Say a sincere thank-you to someone who serves you, and say a gentle word to yourself too.

cards.v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
cards.a: In conversation, give the other person the chance to speak and listen all the way through.

cards.t: Look Also to the Interests of Others
cards.v: each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
cards.a: Remember something a friend is going through, and ask how he or she is doing this week.

cards.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
cards.a: When someone is talking, put your phone down and listen for five minutes without interrupting or rushing to give advice.

cards.v: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
cards.a: Today, pray first for the church, missionaries, or people in need, and then for your own needs.

cards.t: Whom Have I in Heaven but You?
cards.v: Whom do I have in heaven? There is no one on earth whom I desire besides you.
cards.a: Say to the Lord: You are my satisfaction. Then do one good deed that needs no one else's company.

cards.v: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
cards.a: While you wait, tell the Lord three things you are thankful for today.

cards.v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
cards.a: Choose one person near you today and love them once the way Jesus loves you.

cards.v: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
cards.a: After praying, say one thing that needs to be said, gently and clearly.

cards.v: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
cards.a: Say to the mirror: Thank You, God, that I am Your wonderful creation.

recon.safety: If this involves violence, control, threats, stalking, sexual coercion, humiliation, blackmail, or any crime, do not face it alone, and you do not need to "talk to them privately" first. Make sure you are safe first, reach out to someone you trust, a pastor, or a professional organization, and call the police if necessary. Being hurt is not your fault; it is permitted to leave danger. Forgiveness does not mean silence, and reconciliation does not mean returning to danger. If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number (911 in the US). In the US, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. Outside the US, contact local emergency services or a trusted pastor or counselor.

steps.v: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
steps.d: First take the plank out of your own eye. What did I do wrong in this? How much pride, hurt, or judgment is in my heart?
q: What is my part in this?
Do I want to win this person, or just win the argument?

steps.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
steps.d: Be quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to anger. Give yourself at least one night to bring your emotions and your own faults to the Lord, and ask the Holy Spirit to rule your heart and your mouth.
q: What do I need to confess to God?
Am I willing to pray a blessing over the other person?
What is the Holy Spirit reminding me of?

steps.v: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
steps.d: When it is just the two of you, speak with humility, with specifics, and without accusation. Apologize first for your own part, then share how you feel. The goal is to win the person. (If the other person has a record of violence, control, or threats, do not face them alone. Ask a pastor or a professional to accompany you, or make sure you are safe first.)
q: Can I apologize first for my part?
What is the one specific thing I want to say?
Am I ready to listen to the other person's perspective?

steps.v: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
steps.d: If the other person is unwilling to talk, you may invite one or two mature, fair people whom both of you trust. The purpose is not to add pressure but to help each of you see clearly.
q: Have I sincerely done the previous step?

steps.v: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
steps.d: If it still cannot be resolved, go through appropriate formal channels (a pastor, community mediation, a supervisor, professional help) rather than spreading it in group chats or behind someone's back. "If it is possible, as much as it depends on you, be at peace with all men."
q: Am I going through the right channels?

steps.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
steps.d: Forgiving means letting go of the right to collect a debt and handing judgment over to God. Trust can be rebuilt slowly as the other person changes. When necessary, you can forgive and still keep a safe distance.
q: Am I willing to say, "Lord, I choose to forgive"?
What healthy boundaries do I need to set?

opens: I'd like to start by apologizing for my part: ...
I care about our relationship, so I'd like to talk with you about something.
When ... happened, I felt ... I'd like to hear your thoughts.
I may have misunderstood you. Could you help me understand?
Thank you for listening to me. Can we work on this together?

fruits.d: Love those who are hard to love
Rejoice sincerely in others' good news, without comparing
Take the first step to mend relationships, without striving
Give each other time to grow
Show grace first, and hold no grudges
Keep doing good without losing heart
Do what you say, with no hiding or deceiving
Answer gently and restore others gently
Guard your eyes, your emotions, and your phone

way.t: The Holy Spirit Is My Guide
way.q: Before spending time with this person, did I ask the Holy Spirit first?
How can I treat him or her in a biblical way?
How would Jesus love this person?
Am I relying on the Lord's love, or on my own charm and tactics?

way.t: Let Jesus Receive All the Glory
way.q: Who will receive the glory for the fruit of this relationship?

five.intro: Write down five people who walk with you in your love life, pray for you, and hold you accountable: spiritual companions, mentors, mature friends, or family. Pray for one of them each day, and share an update with one of them each month. You do not have to walk this road alone.

steps.d: Pray for them every day, thanking God for placing them in your life.
Tell them one thing you thank God for about them.
Honestly share your recent relationship situation and struggles.
Ask for their input before making important decisions.
Invite them to ask you: Did you keep your boundaries this week?
Accompany one another, and become a companion to others too.

prays.p: Lord, help us encourage one another, as iron sharpens iron.
Lord, let me not walk this road alone, but with others beside me.
Lord, give me wise counselors, and make me willing to listen to advice.
Lord, help us comfort one another and build one another up.
Lord, make me willing to confess to my companions and pray for one another.

tips: For a first meeting, choose daytime and a public place, and keep it simple.
Pray before you go, and tell a trusted friend your plans.
Arrange your own transportation; don't depend on the other person for a ride.
Remember your boundaries, and tell your companion about them beforehand.
Listening matters more than performing; you don't need to pretend to be someone else.
Don't rush to declare or promise anything; give each other time to get to know one another.
Watch for warning signs: control, belittling, pressure, secrecy, loss of emotional control. If you feel uncomfortable, you can leave at any time.
Afterward, let your companion know you are safe, and honestly reflect: Did I guard my heart?

checks: The first thing I do in the morning and the last thing I do at night is look at my phone.
I keep checking the other person's activity or last-online time.
When my message is read but not answered, I feel anxious or angry.
After seeing other people's love lives, I often feel I'm not good enough.
I have said things in messages that I would never say face to face.
I use scrolling or chatting to escape loneliness, anxiety, or boredom.
I have sent or received messages or photos that made me uncomfortable or crossed my boundaries.
I spend less time with God and with family and friends than I spend on social media.
tips: Choose a regular time each week for a "digital Sabbath": turn off notifications and return to God and the people around you.
After waking, pray and read a Bible verse before you open your phone.
For the hour before bed, keep your phone somewhere other than beside your bed.
Before sending a message, ask three questions: Is it true? Is it gracious? Does it build up?
Unfollow accounts that make you compare or leave you uneasy.
Don't send or accept photos that cross your boundaries. If you face threats or blackmail, keep the evidence and seek help.
